section: Letter from the Chief Executive Officer
text:
Dear shareholders,

2025 was a year of disciplined growth for Kirana. Revenue rose 10.0% to THB 8,420 million and net profit reached THB 531 million. We expanded our cold-chain capacity in Indonesia, where demand from grocery and pharmaceutical customers continues to outpace supply.

Our fleet transition accelerated. We added 96 electric trucks during the year, mostly in Bangkok and the Klang Valley, and installed rooftop solar at six more facilities.

The fourth quarter tested our network. Severe flooding in southern Thailand closed sections of the main southern highway for several weeks and forced us to reroute line-haul traffic. Our teams kept customers informed and service recovered by December. I want to thank every colleague who worked through those weeks.

Looking ahead, we will open four new facilities in 2026 and continue to invest in automation, data and our people.

Arunee Wongsakul Chief Executive Officer Bangkok, 20 February 2026

text:
Revenue grew for the third consecutive year, supported by new contract logistics customers in Indonesia and higher e-commerce parcel volumes in Thailand. Gross margin improved as warehouse utilisation rose.

Capital expenditure increased to fund cold-chain racking, electric vehicles and solar installations. Net debt rose accordingly but remains within our internal limit of 2.0 times EBITDA.

Revenue figures are reported in Thai baht. Indonesian, Vietnamese and Malaysian revenues are translated at average exchange rates for the year.

text:
We delivered 41.6 million parcels in 2025. Full-year on-time delivery (OTD) was 94.0%, measured as the share of shipments delivered within the committed window.

Performance dipped in the fourth quarter. Flooding in southern Thailand closed sections of the main southern highway, and line-haul to Hat Yai was rerouted through slower inland roads. Service recovered in December once the highway reopened.

Warehouse productivity, measured in order lines picked per labour hour, improved 8% year on year following the roll-out of goods-to-person robotics at Lat Krabang and Cikarang.
header: [Kirana Logistics Group Annual Report 2025 | p6 | text: Operations]
[Kirana Logistics Group Annual Report 2025 | p6 | figure: Operations]

text:
At the end of 2025 we operated 37 warehouses. Table 2 lists the 23 major facilities of 8,000 square metres or more; smaller satellite sites are not listed. Utilisation is the average share of usable pallet positions occupied during the year.

Our network strategy is to keep a large hub near each capital city, supported by cross-dock sites that shorten last-mile distances in secondary cities. Cold-chain capacity is the fastest-growing part of the network, and the Cibitung cold store in Bekasi operated close to full capacity for most of the year.

We review utilisation monthly. Sites that remain below 65% for two consecutive quarters are placed on a consolidation watch list, while sites above 92% trigger an expansion study.

Thailand and Malaysia are connected by road through the Hat Yai cross-border lane. Freight between Thailand and Indonesia moves by sea.

text:
Our electric fleet grew from 136 vehicles at the end of 2024 to 218 at the end of 2025, an increase of 82. Electric vehicles now make up 18% of the fleet. All new light trucks ordered for urban routes in Thailand and Malaysia are electric.

Our target is a 30% reduction in emissions intensity per parcel by 2030, measured against the 2023 baseline. Rooftop solar now supplies 31% of the electricity used in our warehouses.

text:
Women held 38% of management positions at the end of 2025, up from 34% a year earlier. We delivered an average of 26 hours of training per employee.

Our lost-time injury frequency rate (LTIFR) improved to 0.42 per million hours worked, from 0.55 in 2024. There were no work-related fatalities. Forklift pedestrian separation was completed at all major facilities.
header: [Kirana Logistics Group Annual Report 2025 | p10 | text: People and safety]

text:
• Fuel prices. Diesel represented 27% of our cost of services in 2025. Fuel surcharges recover most, but not all, increases within one to two months.

• Customer concentration. Our ten largest customers generated 41% of revenue.

• Currency. A weaker Indonesian rupiah reduces the baht value of our Indonesian earnings.

• Extreme weather. Flooding and storms can close roads and facilities, as the fourth quarter of 2025 showed.

• Cybersecurity. A ransomware attempt in June 2025 was detected and contained with no customer data lost.

• Regulation. Changes to electric-vehicle incentives in Thailand could raise the cost of our fleet transition.
header: [Kirana Logistics Group Annual Report 2025 | p11 | text: Principal risks]

text:
We expect revenue growth of 11% to 13% in 2026. Planned capital expenditure is approximately THB 1,050 million.

• Open four new facilities: two in Indonesia, one in Vietnam and one in Thailand.

• Add 120 electric light trucks, bringing the electric share of the fleet above 25%.

• Extend goods-to-person robotics to Surabaya and Binh Duong.

We do not plan to enter any new country in 2026.
